summary_paragraph: A man with HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and GJ tube dependence was admitted for septic shock likely from a urinary tract infection, with concern for concurrent pneumonia. He presented with hypoxia, tachycardia, and hypotension, requiring vasopressor support and ICU care. Initial treatment included broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to linezolid for VRE UTI and cefepime for Pseudomonas pneumonia based on culture results. A malpositioned PICC line was repositioned successfully. He stabilized, returned to baseline, and was discharged to extended care with a two-week course of IV cefepime, oral linezolid, and oral vancomycin, along with continuation of all chronic medications including antiretrovirals and seizure prophylaxis.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
